summary: ISO-NE files the 30-day informational report the E-11 order required. It finds New England long on supply, relies on competitive markets, and proposes a bring-your-own-new-generation rule for large loads and their exclusion from the Installed Capacity Requirement.

points.point: ISO-NE says New England has been flat or declining in load and has not yet seen significant large load growth.
points.quote: New England has not yet encountered significant load growth attributable to the addition of large loads, such as data centers.

points.point: ISO-NE's guiding view is that existing competitive markets can meet upcoming resource adequacy needs.
points.quote: ISO-NE believes that New England’s markets are sufficiently mature and flexible to meet upcoming challenges.

points.point: Pending projects include a lower Pay for Performance rate, capacity auction reforms, uncertainty reserves and demand flexibility.
points.quote: the reduction in the Pay for Performance rate; the Capacity Auction Reforms project; improvements to Surplus Interconnection Service; probabilistic forecasting; uncertainty reserves

points.point: ISO-NE says two actions will be needed: large loads bring their own generation and are excluded from the load-side capacity requirement.
points.quote: requiring new large loads to “bring their own” incremental new generation; and excluding new large loads from the load-side requirements of the capacity market

points.point: ISO-NE intends rules similar to SPP's CHILLS, letting large loads take energy until designated resources and upgrades are in place, subject to curtailment.
points.quote: ISO-NE intends to pursue rules similar to the Southwest Power Pool’s conditional high impact large load service (“CHILLS”) rules

points.point: ISO-NE expects to file the detailed bring-your-own-generation and capacity exclusion rules in 2027.
points.quote: ISO-NE anticipates filing the detailed supporting rules implementing this concept in 2027.

throughLine.text: ISO-NE's filing under the E-11 30-day informational report directive on ensuring adequate generation for existing and new large loads; its CHILLS-style conditional service parallels SPP's approach in E-9.
